name: Moncrief's Generalised Taub-NUT Spacetimes
description: Inhomogeneous toroidal vacuum cosmologies with a compact Cauchy horizon.
history: # History¶A compact Cauchy horizon can survive in an inhomogeneous vacuum cosmology. Vincent Moncrief established an infinite dimensional family of such universes in 1981, within the Gowdy solutions on $T^3\times\mathbb{R}$ [moncrief1981nut]. Their compact spatial sections are three-tori, and each member admits an extension of Taub-NUT type beyond its maximal Cauchy development [moncrief1981nut]. The family allows gravitational waves and spatial variation while preserving the horizon [chrusciel2004horizons].¶Two commuting Killing fields generate the toroidal symmetry orbits. The orbit area serves as a time coordinate in the globally hyperbolic region [chrusciel2004horizons]. Two wave amplitudes obey coupled equations for a map into the hyperbolic plane, while first order constraints determine the remaining metric function [chrusciel2004horizons]. Periodicity of the spatial coordinates also imposes an integral constraint on the data [chrusciel1990cim].¶At the horizon, a periodic Killing direction becomes null. Coordinates that combine its angle with the logarithm of areal time extend through the horizon when the metric functions have the required regularity [chrusciel1990cim, chrusciel2004horizons]. On the continued side, that periodic direction is timelike, so its closed orbits are closed timelike curves [moncriefisenberg1983]. The two choices of logarithmic shift lead to inequivalent extensions in the polarised family [chrusciel1990cim].¶Piotr T. Chruściel, James Isenberg, and Vincent Moncrief made the polarised extension conditions precise in 1990 [chrusciel1990cim]. In their torus variables, the logarithmic datum $\pi$ must be everywhere $0$ or everywhere $1$, and the remaining horizon datum $\omega$ must be analytic, for a vacuum extension retaining the polarised Gowdy form across a compact Cauchy horizon [chrusciel1990cim]. They also proved that an open dense set of smooth polarised Gowdy initial data has an inextendible maximal globally hyperbolic development [chrusciel1990cim]. The extendible universes therefore coexist with strong cosmic censorship in that class [chrusciel1990cim].¶Moncrief and James Isenberg proved in 1983 that an analytic vacuum or electrovacuum spacetime containing a compact null hypersurface ruled by closed null generators has a nontrivial Killing symmetry [moncriefisenberg1983]. A constant analogous to surface gravity distinguishes degenerate horizons from nondegenerate ones [moncriefisenberg1983]. In the nondegenerate case, the Killing field changes from spacelike in the globally hyperbolic region to timelike in the acausal analytic extension [moncriefisenberg1983].

related.text: Gowdy's vacuum universes include the toroidal solutions with a compact Cauchy horizon [moncrief1981nut].
Both families admit vacuum extensions across compact Cauchy horizons into regions with closed timelike curves [moncriefisenberg1983].
A compact null direction becomes timelike beyond the horizon, producing closed timelike orbits [moncriefisenberg1983].

coordinates.name: Toroidal Areal Time

parameters.description: Positive coefficient of the logarithmic angular shift.

First wave amplitude. Analytic functions of $t^2$ and $\theta$ near the horizon, periodic in $\theta$, satisfying $b_{tt}+t^{-1}b_t-b_{\theta\theta}=\tfrac12t^2e^{4b}(q_t^2-q_\theta^2)$, $q_{tt}+3t^{-1}q_t-q_{\theta\theta}+4(b_tq_t-b_\theta q_\theta)=0$, and $f_t=t(b_t^2+b_\theta^2)+\tfrac14t^3e^{4b}(q_t^2+q_\theta^2)$ and $f_\theta=2tb_tb_\theta+\tfrac12t^3e^{4b}q_tq_\theta$, with $f(0,\theta)=0$ and $\int_0^{2\pi}f_\theta\,d\theta=0$.

coordinates.convention: The areal coordinate is $t$; subscripts on $b$, $q$, and $f$ denote partial derivatives. Each spatial angle has period $2\pi$.

coordinates.name: Horizon Extension (+)

parameters.description: Positive coefficient of the logarithmic angular shift.
Analytic continuation $B(T,\theta)=b(\sqrt{T},\theta)$ of the areal family, with $T=t^2$.

coordinates.convention: We use $T=t^2$ and $\chi=\psi+\kappa\ln t$, with $\chi$ periodic modulo $2\pi$. The coefficient $H=\kappa^2(e^{2F}-1)/(4T)$ takes its analytic value at $T=0$, and $\delta$ is a positive continuation radius.

parameters.description: Positive coefficient of the logarithmic angular shift.
